findings.requirement: An open question lives only while it stands
findings.what: Check 2: SR-132/EX-2 (a merged branch's open items are withdrawn at the merge) is dropped with the reason that 'the merge-boundary requirement carries what happens to open questions at the merge'. That is not so: P11's four requirements say nothing about open questions at a merge (searched P11 for question, card, withdraw, branch is gone; only 'feat-x's merged version is no longer in flight' and the conflict question appear). The code still does it and tests marked SR-132 in tests/boundary/test_merge_withdraws_cards.py pin it: a merge withdraws the merged branch's open cards, merging the remote copy withdraws them, merging main into a feature branch withdraws nothing, an unmerged fresh branch keeps its cards (the dump shows tests=0 for SR-132, the marks say otherwise). 'Its branch is gone' does not cover a merged branch that still exists (the test merges feat-x without deleting it). Only the 'went in unconfirmed' summary line goes with P11's hold. Add an example: an open question about a branch whose work was merged into main is withdrawn at the merge, and a sync of main into the branch withdraws nothing; correct the drop reason to the summary line only.

findings.requirement: An open question lives only while it stands
findings.what: Check 4 and consistency with P9: example 2 and the assumptions keep 'an open calibration question' (the old trial card, SR-161/EX-2), but P9 retires the trial card ('No trial card asks for labels', trial cards listed under wont, calibration pairs logged scores with owner labels). No such open question exists in v2, so the example cannot be watched. Replace it with a live subject (an open question about a requirement the judge cascade asked, whose requirement is then superseded) and drop 'a calibration question' from the assumption.

findings.requirement: plumb resolves from the recorded intent what it already answers before asking
findings.what: Check 3 and consistency with P1 and P11: the requirement holds several behaviours (withdrawing answered or duplicate open questions in the background; settling a merge conflict, a stale link or an untraced change before it is asked; the unreachable-judge hold, twice, EX-4 and EX-8; reversal; routing a plumb failure to debugging). EX-6 (silent repin of a stale link) repeats P1's 'Drift on linked code is resolved in the turn that makes it', and EX-7's 'two approved records that contradict reach the owner' is at odds with P1's 'two confirmed records contradict and the recorded intent already says which holds: resolved from that intent, owner not asked'. EX-8 (no judge: the issue is held and not put to the owner) is at odds with P11's 'no judge is reachable: the conflict is put to the owner, no recommendation'. Split into 'open questions are withdrawn when the approved records answer them or duplicate them' and 'a conflict or issue is settled from recorded intent before it is asked' (stale links left to P1), and make P11 and P5 agree on the conflict with no judge.

findings.requirement: What plumb cannot settle goes to a debug workflow, the owner last
findings.what: Check 4: several then-clauses are not observable. 'the step is rerun once it is fixed' is conditional and never says who fixes plumb's own failure; 'records what is missing for the agent to restore' gives no place the agent or the owner can see it; 'a debug workflow opens' and 'its progress is shown' name no surface (P13's progress mod? the log?). The statement's 'resolves it when it can' is open-ended. State what the workflow outputs (one plumb line naming the case and its outcome; the agent's text carrying what is missing) and what it may change; 'round limit' should cite P9's setting (three rounds by default). Also check 3: three trigger kinds plus the investigation plus the last-resort question are one requirement with seven examples; the investigation and the last-resort asking could be separate.

findings.requirement: An open question lives only while it stands
findings.what: Check 4: examples 6 and 7 say 'the status is shown' and 'its records are still listed as not yet approved'. P12's status is a one-line status with counts and no list; name the surface (the plain-words /plumb status of P2) or say the count. Example 8 'the question stays, now about the one record left' is also not observable once read-back cards are retired. Example 9 (an answer to a question about a requirement superseded meanwhile is captured against the replacing requirement) has no source record, code or test and belongs to P4's capture rule; keep it only if the owner wants the edge case.

findings.requirement: A principle is asked once and settles the questions that hinge on it
findings.what: Check 2, test-backed behaviour not in an example: tests/understand/test_principles.py asserts that an undone settlement stays open on the next settling run and that the undo reopens a settled card; example 4 only says the question is back. Add 'and a later settling run leaves it open'. Likewise tests/understand/test_auto_withdraw.py asserts a withdrawal is named once (not at later turn ends); example 1 of the first requirement does not say 'once'.

findings.requirement: A principle is asked once and settles the questions that hinge on it
findings.what: Check 7 wording: DEC-067 is retired here with its rule carried by example 7, while P3 also supersedes DEC-067 with its own decision (owner asked only when an edit changes older intent). Say in one place which draft retires it, so it is not superseded twice. The four SRs of the cluster (SR-161, SR-132, SR-162, SR-172) are each superseded exactly once in this file; no finding there.
